profile.stagger_pattern: 7 at-large council seats in two staggered groups. Group A = 4 seats elected in 2013/2017/2021/2025 (terms Jan 1 of even year following through Dec 31 four years later). Group B = 3 seats elected in 2015/2019/2023 (and 2027). Mayor elected citywide to a 4-year term in the same cycle as Group A (2017/2021/2025). August primary in odd years narrows the field; November general elects. Vacancies are filled by City Council appointment for the remainder of the term, and any unexpired remainder extending past the next odd-year election appears on that ballot as a separate 'Partial Term' race.

SHE KEPT THE CHAIR THROUGHOUT her interim mayoralty (Dec 29 2020 - Jan 26 2021): the Jan 26 2021 report still calls her Council Chairwoman while she was interim mayor, so no one else took over the presidency during that stretch. Bill Bazzi was Council chair PRO-TEM until Jan 26 2021, then Dave Abdallah. Exit: her council term ended Dec 31 2021 (she ran for mayor rather than re-election) and the Council elected Abdallah chair on Jan 11 2022. START DATE 2019-01-01 is the panel-window boundary, not a sourced organizational date - she is sourced as chair from May 2019 onward; the meeting at which she was first elected chair was not retrieved.

Verbatim: 'The Dearborn Heights City Council selected its new Council chairperson and Council chairperson pro tem during its Jan. 11 City Council meeting. Abdallah had been acting as Council chair pro tem since last January, when Bill Bazzi was appointed mayor.' Dated council-record account of the selection vote. Verbatim (Feb 16 2024): 'Everybody's lawyered up,' Council Chairman Mo Baydoun said during the meeting on Tuesday.' Corroborated repeatedly: 'Council Chairman Mo Baydoun' (AAN Jul 19 2024, https://arabamericannews.com/2024/07/19/council-chairman-former-police-chief-respond-to-recent-news-article-claiming-racial-discrimination-in-dearborn-heights/); 'Dearborn Heights City Council President Mo Baydoun' (AAN Feb 21 2025); 'Dearborn Heights Council Chairman Mo Baydoun' (AAN Mar 15 2025); 'Council Chairman Mo Baydoun has assumed the role of acting mayor' (AAN Oct 8 2025). EXIT: vacated the chair on becoming acting mayor after Bazzi's Oct 8 2025 resignation; Hassan Ahmad took over. START DATE CONFLICT: the Feb 21 2025 AAN profile says 'In September 2023, he was elected City Council president, succeeding Ray Muscat, who had resigned.' That cannot be right for the CHAIR - Dave Abdallah is directly sourced as chair in Aug 2023 AND Nov 2023, and Muscat was Council VICE chair / chair pro tem (elected to that post Jan 11 2022) when he resigned Aug 21 2023. The September 2023 election almost certainly made Baydoun chair PRO TEM, not chair, and the 2025 profile conflated the two. Start therefore recorded as 2024-01-01, the start of the new council term after Abdallah's departure; the organizational meeting that elected Baydoun chair was NOT retrieved, so the day-level start is inferred (first direct evidence of him as chair is Feb 13 2024) - entry_mode left 'unknown' for that reason.

Verbatim: 'Hassan Ahmad, who assumed the role of Council chair following Baydoun's transition to mayor, led the field with 5,154 votes' and 'City Council Chair Hassan Ahmad topped a competitive field of five candidates.' He was still 'City Council Vice President'/'Council vice chair' as of Feb 2025 and Oct 10 2025 (https://arabamericannews.com/2025/10/10/dearborn-heights-election-four-local-races-to-shape-the-citys-political-future/), so the handover falls between Oct 8 and Nov 7 2025; start recorded as 2025-10-08, the date Baydoun vacated - DAY-LEVEL DATE INFERRED, month solid. Continued into the new term: sworn in as 'City Council President Hassan Ahmad' at the Jan 17 2026 inauguration (https://arabamericannews.com/2026/01/23/dearborn-heights-mayor-mo-baydoun-sworn-in-vows-new-era-of-services-safety-and-lasting-flood-solutions/), and 'City Council Chairman Hassan Ahmad' as of Aug 6 2026, which also states 'Ahmad has served as a City Councilman since being elected in 2020 and was appointed Council chairman in 2025' (https://arabamericannews.com/2026/08/06/hassan-ahmad-appointed-to-wayne-county-commission/ - note the paper's '2020' is itself wrong; he was elected Nov 2 2021). PENDING DEPARTURE: that Aug 6 2026 article reports Ahmad appointed to the Wayne County Commission, with Mayor Baydoun saying 'we will be losing him on the City Council'; no effective date for his council/chair departure is given and he remained on the city roster as of Aug 17 2026, so this tenure is left ongoing.

Established odd-year Aug primary / Nov general; 7 at-large council seats split 4 (2017/2021/2025, same cycle as mayor) and 3 (2019/2023). Confirmed by the 2013 AAN headline 'Dearborn Heights voters to choose Mayor, four council members', the 2023 Patch primary piece ('Eight candidates are running for three Dearborn Heights City Council seats'), and the 2025 AAN preview ('Five additional candidates will compete in a tight race for four open seats on the seven-member City Council'). The August primary is conditional, not automatic: in 2025 there was NO council primary because only five candidates filed for four seats - 'Under Michigan election law, primaries are omitted when the number of candidates does not exceed double the number of openings.'

Rung 4 (local newspaper) carried the entire city. arabamericannews.com is fully fetchable by curl INCLUDING its ?s= site search, which returns dated permalinks - this made cycle-by-cycle retrieval nearly free of WebSearch quota. Every cycle 2017/2019/2021/2023/2025 plus all six mid-term events sourced from AAN. patch.com also fetchable (used for the 2023 primary). ballotpedia.org WAS fetchable by curl (200, 130KB) but its Dearborn Heights page carries no municipal roster.

SIX mid-term changes found and dated, of which FOUR are council seats, not the mayoralty. Mayor: Paletko died 2020-12-29; Malinowski-Maxwell interim by charter (retaining her council seat) to 2021-01-26; Bazzi appointed 2021-01-26 by 4-3 vote; Bazzi resigned Oct 2025; Baydoun acting by charter as Council President. Council: Hicks-Clayton left ~Dec 8 2020 on election as Treasurer, seat deadlocked for seven weeks, Baydoun appointed 2021-01-26; Bazzi's council seat vacated 2021-01-26, Abdel-Hak appointed same night 5-1; Muscat resigned effective 2023-08-21, Abdel-Hak appointed again in Sept 2023; Baydoun's council seat vacated Jan 2026 on becoming mayor, Constan the apparent appointee.

Seat count reconciles at 7 for every year: 2019 = Malinowski-Maxwell/Bazzi/Wencel/Constan + Hicks-Clayton/Muscat/Abdallah; 2026 = Ahmad/Wencel/Bryer/King (2025 cycle) + Malinowski-Maxwell/Saab (2023 cycle) + Constan (appointed to Baydoun's seat), matching the live city roster exactly. Malinowski-Maxwell's disappear/reappear (off council 2022-2023) is a genuine gap in service, not a missed appointment - she lost the 2021 mayoral race and re-won a council seat in 2023; recorded as two separate tenures. Abdel-Hak likewise has two genuinely separate appointed tenures (2021 and 2023). All quoted roster text spot-checked against locally saved HTML rather than against summarizer output.
